Retirology vs. Empower's retirement planner

Empower's free dashboard — formerly Personal Capital — tracks your net worth across linked accounts and includes a retirement planner. It's free because it's the front door to Empower's paid wealth-management service. Retirology costs a little once and is just a planner.

Where Retirology is different

  • No sales funnel. There's no advisory business behind Retirology and nothing to upsell. You pay once and own the app.
  • No account, no linked logins. Your financial data stays in a file on your own computer.
  • Depth on the tax side. The decisions that move an early retirement — Roth conversions, ACA subsidies, penalty-free early access, state taxes, IRMAA — are modeled together every year of the plan.

When Empower is the better choice

  • You mainly want automatic net-worth and investment-fee tracking, for free.
  • You're interested in having a firm manage your investments.

Common questions

Is Empower's retirement planner really free?

The planning and tracking tools are free with an account. Empower also sells advisory services, charged as a percentage of the assets it manages; the free tools are how many clients find it.

Does Empower model Roth conversions or ACA subsidies?

Empower's planner focuses on a Monte Carlo projection from your linked accounts and life events. If detailed Roth conversion, ACA subsidy, SEPP or state retirement-tax modeling matters to you, a dedicated planner like Retirology goes further.

Can I use both?

Yes. Many people use a free aggregator to track balances and enter the totals in a planner a few times a year.
